notes: Version 2.6 corrects four scientific statements and adds a labelled interpretation. (1) A gauge charge, a function constant on the projection fibres, factors through the projection and is therefore a function of the observable state; it is not an observable left unresolved by the projection, and its identification with a conserved physical charge is stated as open. (2) The two continuum hypotheses, a smooth fibre bundle and a differentiable base, do not determine a connection: the same bundle and projection admit connections of different curvature. A structure group, its unitary representation and a connection are now supplied explicitly, distinct from the group of global fibre-preserving automorphisms, and the transport convention and gauge transformation are stated. The admissibility interpretation of the connection becomes a labelled reading, and the paper no longer claims a non-postulated origin of the curvature. (3) Curvature measures the path dependence of transport, not a failure of admissibility, and flatness gives a path-independent identification of fibres only locally, since a flat connection on the circle can have non-trivial holonomy. (4) The uniqueness of the Yang–Mills action is stated under an explicit truncation (total mass dimension at most four, fixed background), with one coupling per abelian factor only in a basis that diagonalises the abelian kinetic matrix; when a charge normalisation fixes the basis, kinetic-mixing entries are additional couplings. The version adds a conclusion with an interpretive outlook, primary references (Yang and Mills; Baez and Schreiber; Tong), a font and Unicode-extraction preamble, and an en dash in the PDF keywords. The supplied SU(2) carrier statement and the Foundation attributions of version 2.5 are unchanged.
